No worries, valid questions. I use the Family Accounts feature primarily for the automation of screen time limits. Rather than have to tell my kids it's time and have the whole "one minute" back and forth, they know that it's automatically enforced. Technology enabling good practices is really nice.

As far as the active monitoring stuff - that's not as important to me today, but it was really useful when I first got my son his own laptop. We've discussed good practices, and we're a very open household about all topics. But with little kids, trust but verify is incredibly important. What you talk about isn't always understood until they gain experiences. It's the same reason I won't let his account be an Administrator, meaning I have to install a lot of things for him.

One example of the value of the monitoring - he was really into Minecraft mods for a while and was downloading all kinds of crap. In the website report, I noticed a URL that looked shady as hell to me. Logged into his account with him and ran CCCleaner - sure enough, all kinds of malware had been installed with a mod installer he had downloaded from one of the hundred different "Download" buttons you find on those sites. Because of the report, I caught the malware early, and he and I together went through the hassle of changing all his passwords and wiping the computer. Lesson learned, but had I not been monitoring he would have been compromised for who knows how long.

I guess the short of it is I view it kind of like a learner's permit - for a while, do what you want though with the oversight of an experienced adult. After you've gained experience and trust, you'll be completely on your own.
